text.p: - Janez Podobnika was elected as the new president of Slovenia's 90-seat parliament on Tuesday after winning a majority of 82 votes out of 86 present members of parliament. Parliament also elected three vice presidents.

- Miran Mejak, leading Slovenia's delegation in succession talks over former Yugoslavia's assets in London, said Yugoslav insistance on being the sole legitimate successor of the ex-Yugoslav federation was unacceptable to Slovenia.

- Slovenian president Milan Kucan at the Organisation for Security Cooperation in Europe summit in Lisbon on Tuesday offered to set up an office in Ljubljana for an ombudsman for public media in Europe.
- Slovakia threatened to demand the exclusion of Slovenia from the Free Trade Agreement because Slovenia did not accept the conditions for liberalisation of its agricultural trade.
- Slovenian employers and trade unions will continue talks on changes to the agreement determining workers' benefits on Wednesday.
- The Christmas tree that will decorate St. Peter's Square in the Vatican is 28 metres high and comes from Slovenian forests.

- About 53 percent of Slovenians support the choice of Janez Podobnik as parliamentary president, some 23 percent oppose it, while the rest had no opinion on the matter, a survey by the newspaper showed.
- Slovenia has 10 organisations for the country's 140,000 disabled. Slovenia's total population is two million.
- Total turnover on the Ljubljana bourse in November fell to 14 billion tolars ($9.9 million) from 29 billion in October.
